South East Water slumps to loss after hefty bill from supply failures

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

It is still to be decided how many of the co-host nations will qualify automatically for the tournament.

The 2035 World Cup bid has also put forward a host stadium in Northern Ireland - Belfast’s Windsor Park - and two each in Scotland and Wales. The Scottish grounds are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road, while the Welsh pair are both in Cardiff: the Millennium Stadium and the Cardiff City Stadium.

The remaining English host stadiums are: Villa Park, The AmEx, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, and the Stadium of Light.

Three more stadia could be added to the bid, most notably a potential new Chelsea ground. Discussions as to the future of Stamford Bridge have been bubbling away for decades as the club’s hierarchy debate whether to redevelop the current ground, knock it down to build a new one on the current site, or move to a new site altogether.

Birmingham City’s new Powerhouse Stadium and Wrexham’s renovated Racecourse Ground could also host matches.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed the news, saying: “The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

“Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.”

FA CEO Mark Bullingham said: “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”

England last hosted a World Cup in 1966, when the men’s team famously beat West Germany 4-2 in the final to seal the nation’s first major honour. The Lionesses have since become back-to-back Euros champions in 2022 and 2025, but suffered World Cup final heartbreak in 2023 when they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in Sydney.

Before the UK’s host bid for 2035 was confirmed at a special FIFA Congress, it was also revealed that a joint bid by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica had been approved to host the 2031 World Cup.

#1739. Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for new signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

Eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

The goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

One of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his new club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

We lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

To lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every big team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

Every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

It was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who showed some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

John McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

Arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

That was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

Maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

Garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

McGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

Suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

Gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

Maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

Eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

Signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

Gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the new signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

Tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

Suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

We’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

Arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

Cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

Maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

Saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

Arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

Arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

Timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Bukayo Saka does seem to be getting a lot of time and space on the right flank.

It’s looking a risky tactic by Villa at the moment as the England international is being invited to cut in towards the penalty area.

Havertz is played down the inside-right channel in the penalty area by a cute Odegaard pass bur he blazes his shot across goal and wide of the left post. A replay shows he was offside but even so it was a lazy finish.

Kamara grabs Tzolis round the waist from behind and when the winger hits the deck, rounds him and passus to Buendia who crashes a right-foot diagonal shot on to the bar from 20 yards. The ref did not see it as a foul despite Arsenal’s protestations but had it gone in it would have given VAR a dilemma.

Worth keeping an eye on Aston Villa midfielder George Hemmings tonight.

He is only a teenager and has emerged from Villa’s academy, but Unai Emery is already a huge fan.

Hemmings produced a highly promising performance in the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Suzuki misjudges the flight of Rice’s typically menacing corner and flaps at it but his defenders and an offside flag leave him without egg on his face.

McGinn stops Calafiori down the left then gives the ball straight to Tzolis. The Greece winger opens his body and passes to Lewis-Skelly who shoots with his right foot from the left of the 18-yard line. Cash slides in to block the shot and it loops over the bar for a corner.

Hemmings uses his strength to hold off Ben White and shift the ball inside to McGinn who wraps his left instep around a shot and wafts it into building site behind Raya’s goal.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are in the directors’ box watching the game. Villa don’t look like a hastily assembled team.

Suzuki knocks the ball long with his left foot, looking for Jackson but the ball spins away from him to Raya who boots it back upfield. McGinn pounces on it, turns past Rice and plays Cash in down the right. He crosses towards the near post and Mosquera hooks it clear.

Arsenal kick off with Odegaard spinning and trying to play Saka in down the right as they defend the empty North Stand end. The ball skids off the turf and Saka can’t trap it. The ball goes out for a Villa throw-in.

Who dies in the summer and played for both clubs.

Arsenal are in fact in yellow and navy. My mistake.

Villa in claret and blue with a twist, the shorts are blue for the first time since, I think 2001. Arsenal are in yellow and black. Leeds, like Arsenal, have traditionally worn yellow and blue as their away strip but have been shunted into yellow and black as well by Adidas this season.

There are a few guys standing in the North Stand with hard hats on, and it appears they are on ball retrieval duty.

They will be on red alert for any wayward shots that land in the empty stand.

Warm reception for Ezri Konsa from Villa’s fans as he walked back to the tunnel with Arsenal’s substitutes.

Konsa joined Arsenal last week for £51m, ending a spell of seven years at Villa Park.

Wonder if the likes of Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez will get a similar reception when they return here with Chelsea.

Aston Villa  Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Barkley; McGinn, Buendía, Hemmings; Jackson. Substitutes  Bizot, Mings, Ruggeri, Garnacho, Abraham, Bogarde, Wan-Bissaka, Edward, Lynch.

Arsenal  Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz. Substitutes  Arrizabalaga, Hincapié, Eze, Gyokeres, Konsa, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes.

Zion Suzuki is one of two debuts for Aston Villa tonight and there is a genuine buzz of excitement around the Japan international.

Suzuki was signed from Parma for £30m as the replacement for Emiliano Martinez and arrives with a stellar reputation.

He’s got big boots – and gloves – to fill, but Unai Emery is convinced he will become a future star at Villa Park.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Good evening. Yes, the first match was not as planned but we must keep going forward. Today we are playing our first home match and I am looking forward. We need to try as soon as possible to get our best individuals fit for a good performance. And today is a good match for us. Ir is difficult but always with our supporters here we feel comfortable and confident. Hopefully we can transmit our positive energy to our supporters.

We lost the first game but it is not a [team full of rookies]. We have experienced players. They play with energy and know how we want to play. We have to adapt with Suzuki but we have confidence [in him]. Jackson, the striker, and other players, George Hemmings, he is young but played fantastically in pre-season. He knows how we want to play.

Today is a challenge but I’m really looking forward to how the players will respond collectively, individually. We know we are changing things but no excuses. We have to perform today, we have to try to adapt the new players, to build our team to get their best today.

I am positive and I am optimistic. The players are ready.

Aston Villa are in a transition period and rebuilding on and off the field.

Unai Emery’s 2.0 have been under construction all summer and there could be 10 new signings in by tomorrow morning.

Villa have of course lost six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final, with Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Emiliano Martinez and Lucas Digne all departing this summer.

The North Stand at Villa Park, which faces the iconic Holte End, is also under renovation and closed down for tonight’s game.

It could be a bit quieter tonight but there is still a mood of optimism among Villa fans, despite such a summer of change.

We have had a real block of training sessions to work on things and prepare for this game in the right way.

We will have time to make changes throughout the game [on why he has picked an unchanged team]. They did really well [against Coventry] and for the game we expect [tonight] they have the right qualities to hurt them and that’s how we start.

They have that [upheaval in personnel] but they have been with Unai for a long time, they are a super well-coached team and we know how tough it is always to come here. We are very conscious of that but also very ambitious.

That’s the way we want to play [with aggression] constantly from the first minute, to suffocate the opponent and be better than them.

[Does it being your 250th Arsenal Premier League game add something special to it?] Just to win [makes it special].

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

Villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

#1738. Man United star Bryan Mbeumo stays up late to play GTA6 on morning of his new boss's first day at work: Athletes' performances to 'plummet' for weeks as Liverpool and Arsenal players reveal their video game all-nighters

Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release

In a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and showed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The new boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9

Conor McGregor announced that he would give employees at various businesses the day off

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the new GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

He told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the new game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor announced that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was launched.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game

'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, said with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a big one.'

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' said Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'

New York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall said. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after big games

Those issues appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony said it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event

Department store chain John Lewis said it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

Manchester City will welcome back Matheus Nunes for their Champions League clash with Napoli on Tuesday.

Enzo Maresca’s side are looking to arrest a slump that has seen them win just one of their last six matches in all competitions.

That victory came by way of a penalty shootout against Brighton in the Carabao Cup, and they were held to a surprise 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium last time out.

One key man they will be without is Antoine Semenyo, who continues to be sidelined with a knee problem that is supposed to keep him out for a total of eight weeks. He could return to action just before Christmas.

As for their returners, Nunes, the versatile Portugal international, gives City another option at right-back.

He had been out with an ankle issue, but is “fine” to face Napoli.

Elsewhere, it looks likely that Maresca will keep mostly the same side, despite the disappointment last weekend.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will continue in goal despite shaky form, and Nunes could come back in at right full-back.

Marc Guehi returned from a hip problem that he saw him withdraw from the recent England international camp, and he will play alongside Ruben Dias.

Nico O’Reilly was replaced by Josko Gvardiol at the weekend, and it is a toss-up between the pair, with Maresca still undecided on his first-choice left-back.

In the engine room, big-money signing Enzo Fernandez saw himself benched in favour of Ayyoub Bouaddi on Saturday, but he could come back into the side here alongside Elliot Anderson.

#1736. Hansi Flick's blunt Real Madrid claim as Mourinho closes gap

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:38

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has insisted that he is not concerned by Real Madrid's progress under Jose Mourinho, although his comments have taken on added significance after the Spanish capital club drew level on points with their bitter rivals.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, Flick dismissed questions about Madrid's improvement and emphasised that Barcelona were focused entirely on maintaining their position at the top of the table. At the time of his press conference on Saturday, the Catalan giants held a three-point advantage over Mourinho's side.

However, that lead disappeared later in the evening when Real Madrid secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu. Carlos Espi's late winner lifted Los Blancos to 33 points, level with Barcelona, although Flick's team retain first place with a game in hand.

The sequence adds an intriguing dimension to Flick's remarks, made just hours before Madrid reduced the gap to zero. Barcelona now have an opportunity to restore their three-point advantage against Villarreal, but their manager's determination to ignore developments in the Spanish capital will be tested by an increasingly competitive title race.

Asked whether he had expected Real Madrid to improve so significantly under Mourinho, Flick declined to focus on the performances of Barcelona's biggest rivals.

"I don't care about Real Madrid. What they do is none of my business," the German said during his pre-match press conference, as reported by Brazilian outlet Trivela.

He explained that Barcelona's previous meeting with Madrid was already behind them and that his immediate priority was Sunday's home fixture against Villarreal.

"We are three points ahead of them and we want to maintain that position," Flick added. "That's what matters to us, not what Real Madrid are doing or how well they are playing."

Those comments were made before Madrid's victory over Celta and should not be interpreted as a response to Mourinho's latest result. Rather than criticising his Portuguese counterpart, Flick was attempting to shift attention towards Barcelona's own responsibilities in the title race.

The former Bayern Munich manager nevertheless acknowledged the improving standard of competition in La Liga, pointing to several teams capable of challenging the traditional dominance of Spain's two biggest clubs.

"There are also Atletico Madrid and Real Betis, who are having fantastic seasons. La Liga is very strong, that's the truth," he said when discussing Madrid's progress.

Flick was particularly complimentary about Villarreal, describing their head coach Inigo as an exceptional young manager with a promising future. His praise reflected the importance he attaches to Barcelona's next opponents, who could complicate the Catalans' efforts to maintain their advantage over Real Madrid.

While Flick was preparing his players for Villarreal, Mourinho's team faced a difficult evening against Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu.

The visitors made an excellent start, taking the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes. Madrid then missed an opportunity to equalise before half time when Kylian Mbappe failed to convert a penalty, leaving the hosts facing the prospect of a damaging defeat.

Jude Bellingham eventually restored parity in the 66th minute, finishing from inside the penalty area after Mbappe had provided the final pass. Madrid continued to push for a winner and were rewarded when Espi struck in the closing stages, converting the rebound after his initial header had been saved.

The victory was particularly significant in the context of the title race. Mourinho's side had begun the weekend three points behind Barcelona, but their determination to recover from an early setback ensured that the leaders would enter Sunday's fixture without any points advantage.

Madrid have now collected 33 points from 13 league matches, while Barcelona have the same total after 12 games. Flick's men therefore remain in control of their own position, although they will need to overcome Villarreal to re-establish a three-point cushion.

Barcelona were already preparing for a demanding encounter against opponents capable of causing problems for the leading sides, with Flick facing several selection decisions ahead of the fixture. The Catalans are looking to record their 12th league victory of the campaign and preserve their position at the summit.

Flick's refusal to dwell on Madrid's progress is consistent with his emphasis on Barcelona's own performances. Yet Saturday's result has removed their immediate margin for error, giving Sunday's meeting with Villarreal additional importance.

A victory would restore the three-point lead that Flick was referring to during his press conference. Anything less would leave Barcelona and Mourinho's Madrid separated by little or nothing at the top of La Liga heading into the next round of fixtures.

#1733. Bruno Guimaraes reveals Arsenal ‘apology’ after £75m transfer

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Bruno Guimaraes revealed he apologised to the Arsenal squad after joining the club in the summer.

The Brazilian spent five years at Newcastle before completing a £75million move to Arsenal in August.

During his time on Tyneside, Guimaraes had several heated clashed with Arsenal’s midfielders, including Jorginho and Declan Rice.

“I remember the first time I had to speak in front of everyone, the first thing I said was sorry to the boys.” Guimaraes said.

It has been a patchy start to life at Arsenal for Guimaraes, who has had his best moments off the bench as a substitute.

However, the 29-year-old insisted there is still “much more” to come from him, and he is determined to play his part in an Arsenal side challenging on all fronts.

“We push each other to always be playing well, because if you don’t play well, other players will come and play well,” Guimaraes said.

#1732. Carlos Espi leads Europe's super-subs as Jose Mourinho explains role

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:59

Real Madrid striker Carlos Espi has emerged as Europe's most prolific substitute this season, with his latest match-winning intervention prompting Jose Mourinho to explain why the 21-year-old remains such an effective weapon from the bench.

The Spaniard scored the decisive goal in Saturday's 2-1 comeback victory over Celta Vigo, taking his tally to four goals in all competitions without making a single start. No substitute across Europe's five major leagues has scored more this season when domestic and European competitions are combined.

His remarkable efficiency has become increasingly important to Mourinho, whose side needed another late rescue act after falling behind at the Santiago Bernabeu. Yet despite Espi's growing influence, the Portuguese manager believes the forward's particular qualities are better suited to certain situations than to Madrid's usual starting system.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho praised his young striker's attitude and penalty-box instincts, while acknowledging that his current role presents an unusual challenge for a player consistently delivering decisive contributions.

Madrid's victory against Celta offered another demonstration of why Espi has become such a valuable alternative to Kylian Mbappe.

The visitors took the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes, and Madrid's difficulties deepened when Mbappe fired a first-half penalty over the crossbar. Mourinho introduced Vinicius Junior after the interval, with the Brazilian helping transform the hosts' attacking performance.

Vinicius initiated the move that allowed Jude Bellingham to equalise in the 66th minute, combining with Mbappe before the England midfielder finished from inside the penalty area. With the game still level heading into the closing stages, Espi delivered the decisive contribution.

The youngster attacked a Vinicius cross in the 85th minute and saw his header saved by Ionut Radu, but reacted quickest to the rebound to put Madrid ahead.

It was his third winning goal in La Liga this season, following similarly decisive interventions against Espanyol in August and Elche in September. All three arrived after he had entered the pitch as a substitute, turning matches that were heading towards draws into victories.

Those four goals have established the former Levante striker among Europe's most effective impact players, despite his limited opportunities. The £21m summer signing has already made a greater contribution than many might have anticipated when he arrived at the Bernabeu, particularly given the presence of Mbappe, Endrick and several other attacking options in Mourinho's squad.

His latest intervention also carried considerable significance in the title race. Madrid's victory moved them level with Barcelona on 33 points, although the Catalan club retained first place with a game in hand ahead of Sunday's encounter with Villarreal.

While Espi's scoring record could strengthen calls for a starting opportunity, Mourinho believes his effectiveness is closely connected to the circumstances in which he enters matches.

"Some players have specific characteristics," the Real Madrid coach explained after the Celta victory. "I don't want to say that Carlos won't start, or that Carlos can't play 90 minutes, because he can."

Mourinho pointed to the difference between Madrid's usual attacking approach and Espi's more traditional centre-forward profile. His team generally favour combination play and attacking runs into space, whereas the Spaniard thrives when opponents retreat towards their own penalty area.

"He's a guy with great quality in the box, a guy who's good in the air, a guy who plays well with his back to goal," Mourinho added, praising the striker's movement towards both posts.

The manager believes Espi becomes particularly dangerous when Madrid sustain pressure against opponents defending deep, allowing him to attack crosses and second balls inside crowded penalty areas.

That explains why Mourinho has repeatedly introduced him during the closing stages of difficult matches, often accepting a less balanced formation to increase his team's attacking presence.

The Portuguese coach also addressed the possibility of partnering Espi with Mbappe from the start, explaining that such an arrangement would require the wide players to take on greater defensive responsibilities. With Madrid's current attacking personnel, he does not believe a conventional 4-4-2 would provide the necessary balance.

Nevertheless, Mourinho insisted that the forward's status is not permanent and expressed his desire to reward him with greater opportunities.

#1730. Arsenal's dynasty drive behind their raft of new contracts: Why stars are desperate to play for Mikel Arteta, the ultimatum he gives each of them and the dilemma over whether to extend Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz

Published: 07:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 19 November 2026

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer. Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s new four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

News of new contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours. Extending players when they're approaching the final two years of their contract isn't revolutionary, but the spate of them in such quick succession drew the eye.

Most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s new contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on new contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree new terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

He told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

Now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The plan to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

The biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

The injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

Kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next big decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

Havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain important to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

Mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

Given most of the players who have agreed new long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Big Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

The environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be said for stars at every club in the league.

There’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

When Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his new midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager said: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement

The collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal

This season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

Much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

#1728. The Chelsea problem Xabi Alonso cannot ignore - and who is really to blame

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

There is no defending Chelsea, because again there was simply no defending by Chelsea.

One goal up and with home advantage against a Leeds team they had already beaten at Stamford Bridge this season in the Carabao Cup, Xabi Alonso and his players took that encouraging platform for success and ripped it up, deservedly losing 4-1.

At least Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United could play the “we only had 10 men” card.

Whatever is failing to function right now at Chelsea is a complex web spun by poor decision-making and performances from a whole host of implicated parties.

The Chelsea defence showcases the Blues’ endemic struggles for consistency in a perfect microcosmic form, not least because there are so many stakeholders who must each accept their share of the blame.

An injury record peculiarly problematic for a team largely only playing once a week this season in the absence of any European football has left them without captain Reece James, summer signing Maxence Lacroix and the improved Jorrel Hato - players whose availability might not cure all their defensive ills, but would certainly help.

Their absences mean more minutes for players not showing any signs that they possess the composure or robustness needed to provide support for a potent attack and secure a return to the Champions League.

Malo Gusto was beaten twice for Brenden Aaronson’s run to goal for Leeds’ fourth - something that happens all too often for a player valued by Chelsea at £75million in the summer transfer market.

Wesley Fofana remains a liability, and his £75m transfer fee back in 2022 - £89.2m adjusted for inflation - surely makes him the worst pound-for-pound signing Chelsea have made in the BlueCo era.

And while Josh Acheampong, 20, has been the one Chelsea defender to draw consistent praise in the first three months of the campaign, he was suspect against Leeds.

So too was Levi Colwill, a player with enormous potential but who has so far failed to rediscover his physicality and form since the torn anterior cruciate ligament that kept him sidelined for almost all of last season.

A question it is worth Alonso and his coaching staff asking themselves: is 34-year-old Emi Martinez clearly a better goalkeeper than Mike Penders, the inevitable long-term No1?

There is a case to be made to fully blood Penders now, whatever promises might have been made to Martinez when he joined. The Argentine currently looks a shadow of the commanding player he was at Aston Villa.

Wesley Fofana must surely be Chelsea’s worst pound-for-pound signing in the BlueCo era

Individual errors from Fofana and Gusto and the softness of Colwill and Martinez mean plenty of the blame is rightly being portioned in their direction, but other parties are just as culpable.

Alonso, for example, has flattered to deceive as manager so far, switching between a back three and a back four with the result that his team look capable of playing neither, not both. His Chelsea side have scored a laudable 20 league goals but conceded a lamentable 20 at the other end.

Responsibility also lies at the boardroom door, where questionable recruitment has taken place. Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi were not at the standard required and have taken too long to move on (still neither player has permanently left the club).

And while he is far from the complete product, Trevoh Chalobah had been one of the more consistent centre-backs of the Clearlake era yet was moved on to high-flying Como this summer in favour of handing a greater amount of game time to Fofana.

If Chelsea are to get back to the pinnacle of English football, which is where the club sees itself, then recruitment, coaching and player performances must all improve.

Accepting shared responsibility is the first step towards revamping and properly rebuilding a defence that simply isn’t going to deliver Champions League football on current form.

#1727. Transfer news LIVE: Shock Arsenal move, Kroupi twist; Man Utd want Toney; Chelsea double deal; Liverpool latest

The January transfer window is fast approaching as the likes of Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham all strive to set up some major mid-season signings. Arsenal are being linked with a shock swoop for Jamal Musiala, while we wait to see if Mikel Arteta will move for a new goalkeeper amid the injury to David Raya. The Gunners could face serious competition from Paris Saint-Germain for Eli Junior Kroupi, while they are said to be interested in a deal for Tornike Kvaratskhelia - the younger brother of Khvicha.

Manchester United are expected to launch a move for Ivan Toney after their humiliating start to life under Mauricio Pochettino, who wants to bolster his abysmal defence with a swoop for Fulham’s Calvin Bassey. Chelsea could move for both Alex Scott and Lamine Camara to solve Xabi Alonso’s midfield woes, with the Blues and Arsenal both said to have Cesc Fabregas in mind as their next manager.

Liverpool are rumoured to be eyeing Real Madrid star Endrick, while Tottenham are believed to have agreed a new contract with teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Paris Saint-Germain could step up their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi after Desire Doue suffered a serious knee injury, Teamtalk claims.

The injury comes just a month after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered an ACL injury that is expected to keep him out for at least 6 months.

Kroupi is seen as the next starlet in France and PSG could act in January given their injuries.

Paris Saint-Germain are preparing to offer midfielder Vitinha a new contract until 2032, according to Nico Schira.

The Portuguese’s agent, Jorge Mendes, is thought to be braced for an approach from the European champions.

Sky Germany reports that Bayern Munich are weighing up a move for Schalke 04 goalkeeper Loris Karius.

However, the 33-year-old says he hasn’t spoken to anyone about a potential transfer.

Diario Sport claims that Barcelona now face competition from Chelsea, Manchester United and Manchester City for FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad.

Barca have been leading the race for the 18-year-old, but Twente’s asking price of over €20million could complicate a January move.

Manchester United have hired former Arsenal coach Sam Wilson, who has already started work as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff, writes Matt Verri.

Wilson left Arsenal in the summer, having been at the club for 12 years.

He was the lead physical performance coach under Mikel Arteta up until the end of last season, playing his part in Arsenal’s Premier League title-winning campaign.

Wilson left the Gunners as part of the club’s overhaul of their medical department, with significant changes made in an attempt to address the injury problems that have hindered the squad in recent seasons.

Chelsea could potentially sign both Alex Scott and Lamine Camara in January.

The Blues are on the hunt for midfield reinforcements after losing Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City on summer deadline day and seeing a move for Monaco’s Camara fall through at the 11th hour.

Bournemouth’s Scott has become their No1 target amid a fierce transfer battle with Liverpool, while both clubs are also said to retain an interest in Camara.

TEAMtalk report that Chelsea have not ruled signing both players in January.

Manchester United are said to be pondering a January move for Ivan Toney.

The England striker is believed to be keen on returning to the Premier League in 2027 after a year-and-a-half in Saudi Arabia with Al-Ahli.

Several clubs are said to be interested in Toney, with Football Insider stating that Manchester United are being kept closely informed of the situation.

TEAMtalk claim that Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham and Crystal Palace have also been made aware of the availability of the former Brentford frontman, who could be signed on an initial loan deal that includes an option to buy.

Arsenal have a long-term interest in Jamal Musiala, reports claim.

Musiala’s Bayern Munich future has been thrown into doubt of late as he receives ongoing treatment for a neurological dysfunction that saw him faint twice during pre-season friendlies over the summer.

He has only played once since September 18 due to a muscle injury, leading to suggestions that Bayern no longer view his substantial wages as feasible amid public criticism from global players’ union FIFPRO.

According to talkSPORT, Arsenal and Liverpool both hold a long-standing interest in Musiala, with Chelsea also linked with his services in the past.

Calvin Bassey has confirmed he is in talks over a new contract with Fulham, amid interest from Manchester United.

As reported by Standard Sport earlier this week, 26-year-old centre-back Bassey, was expected to be a transfer target for Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window.

Defence is a key area to strengthen for Man Utd, and Fulham captain Bassey has an admirer in Pochettino.

But Bassey, who is in the third year of a four-year contract at Fulham, is happy in west London and ready to commit his future to the club.

Fulham, who hold the option of extending Bassey's contract by a further 12 months, are keen to keep hold of Bassey, especially after Alvaro Arbeloa promoted him to captain in the summer.

Confirming Standard Sport's reporting, Bassey told TNT Sports: "We’re still negotiating, we’re still talking and obviously it’s an amazing place to be.

"I’ve settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. So, it’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations.”

Bruno Fernandes has revealed that talks over a new Manchester United contract have ended.

The club captain is said to have rejected two offers from Man Utd to extend his current deal, which is set to expire at the end of the season though the club have the option to extend by an extra 12 months.

But the decision has been made to put discussions on hold as he believes the club's priority should be returning to winning ways.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side.

“I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

#1726. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn

The 21-year-old midfielder who came through the ranks at Real Madrid has been signed from Stuttgart.

Brighton’s sporting director Mike Cave said: “We’re delighted to welcome Chema to the club. He has an excellent pedigree having come through at Real Madrid; he followed that with a very good season with Stuttgart last season.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

Fernandez says: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

Chelsea could have subsequently pulled the plug on Enzo Fernadez's move to Manchester City but decided to keep their word. High drama late in the window. https://t.co/NsyIeP1yYO

Chelsea had reached full written club-to-club agreement with Monaco for Camara. But having renegotiated the Balogun deal to Everton, Monaco have withdrawn the agreement with Chelsea for Camara. Fair to say Chelsea are absolutely fuming and regard it unprofessional behaviour.

Tosin said: “I’m in an important part of my career and speaking to the Head Coach and knowing the type of football he wants to play, I think it’s a very good fit. He wants the team to play with courage and that’s something that I always look to do.
