#1689. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#1688. AC Milan Women 3-2 Sassuolo: Grimshaw crucial after crazy first half

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

The veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

Angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

Suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

#1686. Prediction: Feyenoord vs Porto

Feyenoord and Porto meet at De Kuip on Tuesday night with both clubs under pressure to revive their Champions League campaigns.

Having collected just three points from their opening four league-phase matches, the Dutch side sit 32nd in the 36-team table, while Porto are only slightly better off in 26th place. With the knockout rounds already beginning to drift out of sight for both teams, victory could prove pivotal.

Feyenoord head into the contest in poor form and desperately searching for a positive result after six matches without a win in all competitions.

Their latest setback came at the weekend when they were beaten 3-2 at home by Excelsior, a result made all the more painful by the fact it marked Excelsior’s first league victory at De Kuip in 46 years. Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side began brightly through an early goal from Givairo Read, but three unanswered goals left Jan Plug’s late strike as little more than a consolation.

The defeat followed a 5-3 loss away to Heerenveen and a 3-0 home defeat to Inter Milan in the Champions League, meaning Feyenoord have conceded at least three goals in each of their last three matches.

Defensive concerns have become a major issue. The Dutch club have now lost 10 of their last 13 European fixtures and have conceded the opening goal in each of their last seven Champions League outings. That sequence includes defeats against Barcelona, Real Betis and Inter Milan, with their only victory in the current campaign coming against Como.

With memories of last season’s disappointing Europa League campaign, when they finished 29th in the league phase, another defeat would leave their hopes of reaching the knockout stages hanging by a thread.

Anis Hadj Moussa is being assessed after returning from international duty with an ankle injury that forced him to miss the defeat against Excelsior.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is also a doubt after being substituted at half-time on Saturday with a foot problem.

Jakub Moder and Bart Nieuwkoop remain unavailable through injury, while Thomas Beelen, Jordan Bos and Jerry St. Juste are all expected to miss out as well, leaving Van Bronckhorst short of defensive options.

Former Arsenal winger Reiss Nelson made his first start for the club at the weekend, but Luciano Valente could be recalled on the left flank for Tuesday’s encounter.

Porto arrive in Rotterdam with considerably more momentum despite their difficult start to the Champions League campaign.

Francesco Farioli’s side finally claimed their first victory of the league phase on matchday four, producing an emphatic 4-1 win over Napoli. Jan Bednarek, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Omorodion all found the net as the Portuguese side responded impressively after losing their opening three European matches against Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV Eindhoven.

Domestic form has been excellent. Porto have won all 11 of their Primeira Liga matches and already hold a five-point lead at the top of the table. Their most recent outing was less straightforward, though, as they required a penalty shootout to overcome third-tier Paredes in the Taca de Portugal after a 1-1 draw across 120 minutes, due to an extremely unusual own-goal.

The Dragons are competing in the Champions League main stage for the first time in three years and are hoping to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive appearance.

However, their record in the Netherlands offers some encouragement for Feyenoord. Porto have failed to win any of their past four away matches against Dutch opponents, drawing two and losing two. Their previous visits to De Kuip ended in a draw in 1993 and a 2-0 defeat in 2019.

Vasco Sousa remains sidelined with a long-term leg injury. Former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling is struggling with a knee issue and is also ineligible, having not been included in Porto’s Champions League squad.

William Gomes has returned to training after recovering from an ankle problem, but his involvement remains uncertain.

Midfielder In-beom Hwang is set for an emotional return against his former club after joining Porto from Feyenoord during the summer, while striker Santiago Gimenez is also returning to Rotterdam after representing Feyenoord between 2022 and 2025.

Feyenoord’s defensive struggles make it difficult to back the hosts with confidence, particularly against a Porto side carrying significantly stronger form and fresh confidence following their dominant victory over Napoli.

While De Kuip remains a challenging venue and Porto’s historical record in the Netherlands is far from convincing, the visitors appear better equipped to handle the pressure of such a crucial European fixture. Given Feyenoord’s recent performances and recurring defensive issues, Porto look capable of taking advantage and securing an important away victory.

Prediction: Sporting Lisbon vs Manchester United

#1685. Portsmouth vs West Ham United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 22 Nov 2026 12:56, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:06

West Ham United will travel to Fratton Park for the first time in 14 years for Tuesday's Championship clash against Portsmouth.

The Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in 10th place, while the hosts are a point behind in 12th spot in the Championship table.

Portsmouth are sitting four points adrift of the top eight after winning six, drawing five and losing five of their 16 league games this term.

Pompey put together a six-game unbeaten run before they fell to a narrow 2-1 defeat in their most recent home outing before the international break.

John Mousinho's side then returned to action with an underwhelming display in Saturday's 1-1 away draw against Bolton Wanderers, which saw Josh Murphy score the opener with what proved to be Pompey's only shot on target.

Murphy's first goal since March 2025 was soon called out by Sam Dalby as Portsmouth played out a third consecutive away draw after previously taking a point from trips to Wolverhampton Wanderers and Burnley.

Portsmouth will now return to the familiar surroundings of Fratton Park, where they have won four of their last six outings since losing their opening two home games.

That said, they will be looking to tighten up their backline if they are to take anything off the league's highest scorers, having recorded just one clean sheet in their eight outings at Fratton Park

Meanwhile, West Ham have significant work to do if they are to secure an immediate return to the Premier League in their first Championship campaign since 2011-12.

The West Ham hierarchy took the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after being underwhelmed by a return of six wins from the opening 13 league matches of the season.

Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken over the reins, but he is still waiting to secure his first win after over two draws and one defeat in his first three matches.

After starting his reign with a comeback 3-3 draw against Cardiff City, Parker saw his side fall to a narrow 2-1 loss against Blackburn Rovers, before his charges returned from the international break with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Championship's basement side Preston North End.

As a result, West Ham have now gone five games without a win since recording back-to-back away victories over Lincoln City and Swansea City, leaving them three points adrift of the playoff spots and eight points away from the top two.

In search of inspiration, the Hammers can take confidence from the fact they have already beaten Portsmouth at home in the EFL Cup this season, and have won two of their previous three head-to-head away games - a 4-1 success in December 2008 (a game that Parker started) and a 1-0 victory in January 2012.

Mousinho will welcome back midfielder Ebou Adams, who has served his one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Kyle Walker-Peters and Keiber LaMadrid due to muscle and knee problems respectively.

Goalkeeper Alphonse Areola remains a doubt after sitting out Saturday’s draw with an injury he sustained in the pre-match warm-up against Blackburn earlier this month.

Defender Max Kilman is expected to come into the back four after completing his one-match suspension for accumulating five yellow cards in the Championship.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Adams, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Kamara; Shade

#1684. Opposition insight for Milan-Frosinone: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

#1682. Blackpool sack their manager just seven hours after wishing him happy birthday: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'

Published: 15:24 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 16:32 EST, 19 November 2026

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

Evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

Evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm

Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003.

Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card.

Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders.

Whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially announced Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later.

'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the new manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.'

Jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace.

'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.'

Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.'

Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November.

Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

During a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

#1681. Prediction: Sporting Lisbon vs Manchester United

Manchester United turn their attention back to the Champions League on Wednesday night when they travel to the Estadio Jose Alvalade to face Sporting Lisbon.

The visitors arrive in Portugal reeling from another damaging Premier League defeat, while Sporting are in a much healthier position as they continue their pursuit of a place in the Champions League knockout rounds. At the halfway stage of the league phase, Sporting sit 10th in the 36-team standings, seven places and three points above United.

Sporting have made a solid start to their Champions League campaign and remain firmly in the hunt for automatic qualification.

The Portuguese side have taken nine points from their opening four league-phase matches, recording victories over Galatasaray, Lens and Shakhtar Donetsk. Their only setback came in a disappointing 3-2 home defeat against LASK Linz on matchday three.

Their most recent European outing saw them edge past Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, and Sporting now head into this fixture under the guidance of new head coach Paulo Fonseca, who has enjoyed a positive start since replacing Rui Borges earlier this month. Sporting have won both matches under his leadership so far.

Before the international break, the Lions claimed a narrow 1-0 Primeira Liga victory over Moreirense, before a heavily rotated side eased to a 4-0 win over fourth-tier Uniao da Serra in the Taca de Portugal on Saturday. Despite those positive results, Sporting remain nine points behind league leaders Porto domestically.

One statistic will particularly encourage the hosts ahead of Wednesday’s clash. Sporting have scored in each of their last 22 Champions League group-stage or league-phase matches, the longest such run by a Portuguese club.

Sporting are hopeful of welcoming back Zeno Debast and Nuno Santos, both of whom are recovering from muscle injuries, although their involvement remains uncertain.

Fonseca is expected to restore several key players to the starting lineup, including Goncalo Inacio, Ivan Fresneda, Issa Doumbia, Rodrigo Zalazar and Geny Catamo. Chelsea loanee Jesse Derry is also pushing for a place in the side.

Colombian striker Luis Suarez is expected to return after being rested at the weekend. He has scored 13 goals in 15 appearances this season, including four in four Champions League matches.

Manchester United make the trip to Portugal searching for a response after a disastrous start to the Mauricio Pochettino era.

The Argentine watched his side suffer a humiliating 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with United reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro’s controversial early red card. The defeat left the Red Devils 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points, their lowest tally after 11 matches since the 1972-73 season.

Pochettino has publicly acknowledged that the club is involved in a relegation battle and now faces the challenge of tightening a defence that has conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season, more than any other club in Europe’s top five leagues.

European form has been inconsistent for United. They have beaten Sabah and Roma but suffered defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como. The victory over Roma was particularly dramatic, with the Red Devils coming back from two goals down to win 3-2.

United’s away record in the Champions League offers little encouragement. They have won only one of their last 11 away matches in the competition, a 2-0 victory at Villarreal in 2021-22.

There is at least some comfort in the head-to-head record. United have won three of their previous four meetings with Sporting, including both group-stage clashes during their successful 2007-08 Champions League campaign.

United remain without injured trio Manuel Ugarte, Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko. There are also doubts over Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw and reserve goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

The visitors will definitely be without Matheus Cunha, who is suspended after being sent off in the previous Champions League fixture despite scoring the winning goals against Roma.

Matthijs de Ligt endured a difficult outing against Liverpool and could make way for Harry Maguire, with Pochettino expected to retain a three-man defence alongside Leny Yoro and Lisandro Martinez.

In attack, the absence of Cunha could open the door for either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee, while captain Bruno Fernandes is set to face Sporting for the first time since leaving the club in January 2020. Fernandes scored 64 goals in 137 appearances for Sporting and has contributed 21 goals in 29 Champions League matches during his career.

Sporting enter the match with greater stability, better form and significantly stronger defensive foundations than their visitors. Fonseca has made a positive start in Lisbon, while the hosts continue to score regularly both domestically and in Europe.

Manchester United are desperately in need of a morale-boosting result, but their defensive issues have shown little sign of improvement and they now face one of the most consistent attacking sides in Portugal. With Sporting boasting strong Champions League form and United struggling badly away from home, the hosts appear well positioned to collect another important three points.

#1680. Slovan Bratislava vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:08

Slovan Bratislava will be looking to secure their first victory of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign when they host Real Betis at Tehelne Pole Stadion on Tuesday.

The Sky Blues sit bottom of the league phase table with no points from four matches, while Betis occupy 11th place with nine points.

Slovan defeated Celje away from home in the second leg of their playoff-round tie to secure a place in the Champions League main phase, marking a historic achievement for the club.

However, the Slovakian side have found the step up in quality difficult to handle, losing all four of their matches, scoring just once and conceding 17 goals.

Yaya Toure's side began their campaign with a heavy 6-1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain before suffering further losses against Stuttgart, Roma and LASK.

Balancing their domestic and European commitments has also proved challenging, with their continental struggles seemingly affecting their league form, as they sit second in the Slovakian top flight, seven points behind leaders DAC 1904 despite having played a game more.

Perhaps most frustrating for Toure is Slovan's poor home form, with the Sky Blues winless in their last five matches at Tehelne Pole Stadion, drawing three of those encounters.

Real Betis have made a solid start to their European campaign, collecting three wins from four matches while scoring eight goals and conceding six.

El Glorioso opened their campaign with a hard-fought 3-2 victory over Lille, coming from behind to claim all three points.

They followed that up with another thrilling 3-2 win against Porto before beating Feyenoord 1-0 to secure back-to-back home victories.

Manuel Pellegrini's side suffered a narrow 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in their previous Champions League outing, but they have an excellent opportunity to climb the table with a victory over Slovan.

Betis are unbeaten in their last three matches across all competitions and head into this encounter on the back of a 1-1 draw against city rivals Sevilla in La Liga.

Slovan Bratislava form (all competitions):

The switch from a 3-4-3 to a 4-1-4-1 formation has helped Slovan pick up a draw and a victory in their last two matches, and Toure is likely to stick with the same system.

The back four of Sandro Cruz, Svetozar Markovic, Kenan Bajric and Daiki Matsuoka are expected to retain their places, with Peter Pokorny operating at the base of midfield.

Artur Gajdos appeared to pick up an injury in the previous game and could be replaced by Alexej Maros, while Andraz Sporar is set to continue up front, with Roman Cerepaki a doubt due to a back problem.

Real Betis are likely to be without Dani Ceballos, who is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem and is not expected to return to action before the start of December.

Fran Garcia and Hector Bellerin are expected to retain their places in defence, while Diego Llorente could come into the side in place of Marc Bartra.

Antony picked up a knock in the derby but he has travelled with the squad, and should retain his place alongside Isco and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli, with Jose Antonio Morante currently sidelined through injury.

Slovan Bratislava possible starting lineup:

Popovic; Cruz, Markovic, Bajric, Matsuoka; Pokomy, Barseghyan, Ibrahim, Maros, Marcelli; Sporar

Valles; Garcia, Natan, Llorente, Bellerin; Fornals, Bernal; Ezzalzouli, Isco, Antony; Parrott

Slovan have looked like fish out of water in the Champions League this season, and it would take a herculean effort for them to get anything from this encounter, although we expect the hosts to put up a better fight.

Real Betis, meanwhile, have been flying in Europe this season and should be confident of securing their second away victory in the competition as they look to bounce back from their defeat against Dortmund.

#1679. GdS: Milan warned as Bayern Munich could fast-track Tresoldi pursuit amid Kane’s injury

Bayern Munich could make a move for the AC Milan target and Club Brugge star Nicolo Tresoldi, following Harry Kane’s injury.

Tresoldi has been making waves at Club Brugge this season, scoring an impressive five goals in the Champions League, and Milan are one of several big clubs that have been linked with him. Of course, those links are mainly fueled by the fact that the striker is a big Milan fan.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Milan fans know well after Ardon Jashari and Charles De Ketelaere, it’s notoriously difficult to negotiate with Club Brugge. That means a high offer is needed, which is something that could arrive at the Belgian side’s doorstep in January.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Bayern Munich have been keeping an eye on Tresoldi for some time and initially viewed him as a potential signing for the 2027-28 season. However, due to Harry Kane’s ankle injury, they could move much earlier.

The Englishman will be out for at least three months, having had surgery this morning, and that should keep him sidelined until February/March. That puts Bayern Munich in a difficult spot, perhaps forcing them to make a move in January.

Club Brugge want at least €60m for their star and knowing Bayern Munich’s resources, they would be far more comfortable paying that amount than Milan. In short, Kane’s injury has not only resulted in a headache for the German side, but also for the Rossoneri.

#1678. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV

"Since the new manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

The current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

The pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF

There will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

What a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0

St James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

The away side storm forward on the counter as Scott finds Truffert with a piercing pass. The Bournemouth left-back exploits the space vacated by Dedic. Truffert picks out Tavernier with a low cross, but the Englishman’s tame effort is saved by Hornicek. You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

There’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Bournemouth look to have found a rhythm, with Scott dictating proceedings from the centre of the pitch. Truffert has done well early on to deal with Elanga’s attacking threat.

Bournemouth have taken the lead and Newcastle United supporters and [players are furious. Referee Rob Jones appeared to miss a pretty blatant shirt tug from Adrien Truffert stopping Anthony Elanga from spinning away, but that does not excuse the weak defending that led to the visitors scoring moments later.

Lewis Hall was beaten too easily by Rayan whose cross was only half cleared by Malick Thiaw but Amad Dedic got caught ball watching allowing Marcus Tavernier to steal in at the far post to bundle in a deflected shot from Evanilson.

Bournemouth should be two in front. A terrible pass from Sven Botman gifted the Brazilian the ball on the edge of the Newcastle box but he failed to hit the target.

Newcastle are rattled. They have not got to grips with Bournemouth in midfield and they are crowding out Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock whenever Matthias Jaissle’s side look to go direct.

We wondered how Newcastle would match up against Bournemouth and they have looked second best so far.

What a chance for Bournemouth to double their lead! What is Botman doing? The centre-back misplaces a pass and Evanilson latches onto the mistake. The striker runs in on goal, but blazes the glaring opportunity over the bar. That’s a huge let-off for Newcastle. Evanilson must do better from that range.

Scott’s deflected strike richochets into Tavernier’s path, with the Bournemouth attacker sneaking in behind Dedic, who switches off. Tavernier then directs a half-volley into the roof of the net. Newcastle are furious. They feel they should of been awarded a free-kick after a earlier tussle between Truffert and Elanga. Both players are pulling each other’s shirts. After a quick VAR check, the goal stands and the away fans are delighted.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Dedic shows his quality by intercepting a pass from deep, skipping away from Scott’s sliding challenge and then dribbling all the way to the byline. He can’t quite win a corner, but his efforts are appreciated by the Newcastle faithful.

Newcastle attempt to counter through Wissa and Willock, with the latter passing to Barnes. However, the former Leicester man cuts inside and runs into trouble, causing the opening to disappear.

Tavernier takes it and fires a low effort around the wall, but Hornicek is there to get down low and make a relatively routine save.

Elanga has made a busy start to this game. The winger’s pace is so explosive. Bournemouth then win a free-kick on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area as Miley catches Kluivert. Mulitple Bournemouth players are standing over this.

The visitors get us under way at St James’ Park. Which German manager will prevail?

Newcastle are in their iconic black and white strip, while Bournemouth are sporting an eye-catching purple away kit. We are just minutes away from kick-off. St James’ Park is in full voice.

An unchanged line up for Newcastle United in Matthias Jaissle’s third Premier League game as manager but this is a very different sort of challenge.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision-makers. Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1677. Bradford City vs Barnsley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 22 Nov 2026 13:26

Bradford City will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Barnsley to Valley Parade on Tuesday evening.

The hosts currently sit sixth in the League One table, while the visitors are rock bottom.

Bradford made a strong start to the season and were top of the league when head coach Graham Alexander left for Championship side Preston North End.

Since then, Bradford have picked up just one league victory and now occupy the final playoff place on goal difference.

Michael Duff's side drew 2-2 with Doncaster Rovers on Saturday, despite taking the lead twice through Nick Powell and Stephen Humphrys.

Jordan Thomas scored Doncaster's first, before Sean Grehan rescued a point with a dramatic equaliser in the 95th minute.

Duff was not happy with the way his side "just switched off" for Grehan's goal, but insisted there were "a lot of good things" for Bradford to build on.

Barnsley, meanwhile, are in awful form and have picked up just nine points from 14 matches so far, with two wins, three draws and nine defeats.

The Tykes are without a win in their last 11 league games and are sitting four points from safety, having fallen to the foot of the table at the weekend after they lost on Friday and Bromley won on Saturday.

Daniel Stendel's side were beaten 2-1 by Sheffield Wednesday thanks to a Jamal Lowe brace, although Vimal Yoganathan's goal did give Barnsley some hope.

Barnsley have conceded 26 goals in the league so far this season, with only three teams shipping more than them, and they have managed to keep only one clean sheet.

Bradford could hand Humphrys a start after he scored off the bench against Doncaster, with Powell and Antoni Sarcevic providing further attacking support.

Kieran Morgan and Callum Connolly are expected to continue in midfield.

Barnsley are set to welcome back Cameron McGeehan from suspension and he could replace Patrick Kelly in midfield.

Yoganathan is set to continue in the No.10 role, while Makenzie Kirk is expected to lead the line.

McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Pratt; Neufville, Connolly, Morgan, Touray; Sarcevic, Powell; Humphrys

Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche; McGeehan, Connell; Brownlie, Yoganathan, Cleary; Kirk

Barnsley are in woeful form and Bradford should have more than enough to pick up all three points on Tuesday.

#1676. Have Portugal found Cristiano Ronaldo's replacement? Ex-Man City star Carlos Forbs impressed Erling Haaland and stunned Wales this week in No 7 shirt - just over a year after being brutally axed via WHATSAPP

Published: 18:03 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 18:07 EST, 19 November 2026

As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

Portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's new full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo

They are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The new national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

His form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

But it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

The attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

He had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

He was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he said: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the big-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside

'The media made me big, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the plans, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'

But things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

He was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

By the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

If Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he announced himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season

'Today is a dream come true,' he said after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

After 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of new manager Jorge Jesus.

When pressed if he was the new permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he said.

Then he added: 'We know it's a big, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'

It remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

#1675. Newcastle United transfer news: Surprise Nick Woltemade swap deal with Magpies 'interested' in Juventus attacker

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 13:39

Newcastle United are reportedly interested in negotiating a swap deal with Juventus involving Nick Woltemade.

The Magpies earned a spirited 2-2 draw with leaders Arsenal on Saturday evening to end the day in 12th position in the Premier League table.

However, with just three wins in 11 league matches, Matthias Jaissle remains under pressure at St James' Park.

During the summer transfer window, the decision was taken to allow Woltemade to move on loan to Juventus.

That is despite Newcastle having paid £69m for the forward during the 2025 summer transfer window.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Newcastle chiefs are open-minded to allowing the Germany international to remain in Turin on a permanent basis.

Nevertheless, it is claimed that they would like to discuss a potential swap deal involving Francisco Conceicao.

That is despite the Portuguese winger said to remain as a favourite of Juve boss Luciano Spalletti.

Conceicao has contributed just one goal and one assist from his seven starts and two substitute outings in Serie A and the Europa League.

Meanwhile, Woltemade has an impressive five goals and three assists from seven starts and seven substitute appearances in the same competitions.

If Juventus wish to keep Woltemade on a permanent basis, they will need to generate funds or go down the player-exchange route.

Newcastle will not consider selling Woltemade for less than £50m, a figure that Juventus cannot meet at the present time.

Unless the Premier League club take an interest in another Juventus player, the Italian club may have to be open-minded to allowing Conceicao to leave, assuming that Woltemade's return in the final third is viewed more important.
